chart: The stock loss vs the chunked loss on Qwen3.8-27B, one 3,000-token step

memory.stock_note: several [N, V] tables alive at once: BF16 logits, an FP32 copy, the FP32 log-softmax saved for backward, and in backward the gradient of the table; 13.3 bytes per entry measured on the GPU (median over the Qwen3.5 models)
memory.chunked_slice_note: one [128, V] slice in the same copies: 128 x 248,320 x 13.3 bytes
memory.saved_after_forward_note: the one FP32 [N, V] log-softmax table the stock loss keeps for its backward pass (results/saved_activations.json), plus 1.39 GiB of BF16 logits the model returns

procedure_chunked: keep the final hidden states H [N, d] and an empty gradient buffer dL/dH [N, d]
for each slice of 128 positions: logits [128, V] = H_slice x W^T; loss and gradient dL/dZ [128, V] = softmax - one-hot; dL/dH_slice [128, d] = dL/dZ x W, written into the buffer rows; free the slice
after the last slice, backpropagate the filled buffer through the model once
exactness: each token's loss depends only on its own row, so the result is the same: identical loss, gradient norms within 0.04% (measured)

speed.note: whole training step; slice size not tuned

loss_only.note: the loss alone (logits, FP32 cross-entropy, backward to H) on the 27B's shapes (3,000 x 5,120 -> 248,320, BF16, W frozen), RTX 4090, median of 2 x 20 reps; the chunked loop is train_qlora.py's (128-position slices, per-slice backward and float())
